ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangle, and the top horizontal side is labeled as 6 cm. Inside the rectangle there are several circles of the same size: the top row has 3 circles placed side by side, the left and right circles are respectively close to the left and right sides of the rectangle, and the middle circle is gray; the next row has 2 white circles; the bottom has 1 gray circle. The centers of the circles are arranged in the grid shape of equilateral triangles, and the two gray circles are aligned vertically. Reasoning: Because the width of 6 cm at the top is exactly filled by the diameters of the 3 identical circles in the top row, the diameter of each circle is 6÷3=2 cm, and the radius is 1 cm. Adjacent circles are tangent, so the distance between adjacent circle centers is equal to the diameter 2 cm. The problem gives that the circle centers form equilateral triangles, so the vertical distance between the centers of two adjacent rows is the height of an equilateral triangle with side length 2, namely sqrt(2^2-1^2)=sqrt(3). There is one row of circle centers between the two gray circles, so their center distance is 2sqrt(3). The shortest distance between the two circles is equal to the center distance minus two radii, namely 2sqrt(3)-2.

method.method_draft: Read from the image that the labelled 6 cm side is the rectangle's width, and that three congruent circles lie across the top row, tangent to each other and to the two vertical sides. Use the text/image condition that adjacent circle centres form equilateral triangles, so moving from one row of centres to the next has vertical separation equal to the altitude of an equilateral triangle of side 2, namely sqrt(2^2-1^2)=sqrt(3). The two grey circles are vertically aligned with one intermediate row between them, so their centre-to-centre distance is 2sqrt(3). The shortest distance between their circumferences is this centre distance minus two radii: 2sqrt(3)-2.
